messages:
emily-sales: Hey team — FinEdge POC is stuck. They can't see traces in Datadog and are getting intermittent 429s when we forward logs. Can someone help untangle the export and trace-id propagation?

alex-eng: On it. Quick q: FinEdge is on a private deployment (VPC), right? Any custom log forwarder?

emily-sales: Yes private. They're using our log drain -> forwarder -> Datadog (agent on VM). Forwarder is a small Go service. They attached a sample log line: `TRACE=f5a1e2 req=GET /api/pay` but Datadog trace search returns nothing.

priya-se: Two things to check: 1) are we preserving trace headers through the drain (X-Cloud-Trace-Context / traceparent / X-Request-Id)? 2) 429s: likely the forwarder is being throttled by Datadog intake or our log drain rate cap.

matt_s: I asked for logs from the forwarder. Here's the error snippet they sent: 
```
2026-03-18T15:22:03Z ERROR export: post https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/v1/input: 429 Too Many Requests - rate limit exceeded - reset in 12s
```

alex-eng: Ok. Two parallel actions: (A) confirm trace header passthrough config on drain (we've seen autopruning transform rules strip headers before), (B) confirm Datadog API key + intake endpoint + batching settings on forwarder.

priya-se: For header passthrough, they should include this in the drain config: 
```
preserve_headers: ["traceparent", "x-cloud-trace-context", "x-request-id", "x-b3-traceid"]
```
If that's missing, the forwarder never sees canonical trace header and can't link logs->traces.

emily-sales: I asked FinEdge to paste their drain config. They replied: `preserve_headers: []` — so nothing preserved. Oof.

matt_s: That explains the trace gap. Add those headers and redeploy the forwarder. Also, Datadog recommends batching to reduce 429s. Check forwarder sends batches of ~5-10KB or uses the agent which handles retries.

alex-eng: FYI, our log drain also has a burst cap for free-tier customers. For Dedicated/Private POCs we usually bump to 2x burst. I can request a temporary rate raise for FinEdge.

priya-se: Requesting rate bump from platform now. In the meantime, tell customer to enable exponential backoff & jitter in forwarder. Example: 
```
retry_policy:
  max_retries: 5
  backoff: exponential
  initial_delay_ms: 200
  jitter: true
```

infra-bot: Platform ticket created: PLAT-7842 -> TEMP_RATE_BUMP requested for customer FinEdge (requested by alex-eng). ETA 2h.

emily-sales: Great. Also asking them to add this debug endpoint to their forwarder so we can verify header passthrough: `GET /_debug/headers` returns JSON of incoming headers.

matt_s: While we wait, one more check — their collector might be dropping events where the log event size > 256KB. Any huge payloads?

emily-sales: They said no. Typical request/response logs only.

alex-eng: Next steps for FinEdge: 1) update drain config to preserve headers (see snippet), 2) enable batching + backoff in forwarder, 3) run `/_debug/headers` and paste output, 4) we'll apply temporary rate bump. Answer back here once they've redeployed. :thumbsup:

priya-se: If they still don't see traces after header passthrough, we may need to map their internal trace id -> Datadog trace id via our console routing rules. I can pre-check routing rules for their org id.

emily-sales: They're redeploying now. I'll paste results in ~20m. Thanks! :pray:
